summary: Ukiah-area lookout tower on the peak west of town, erected 1930 for the California Department of Forestry; 1930 fire reports survive; listed gone, no site description today.

facts.design: lookout tower with a station building; the papers differ on whether 20 ft is the tower alone or tower plus building
facts.status_note: Index marks it gone; no source describes what remains at the peak today

staffing.status: one observer, M. Hair, named in July 1930; 24-hour service planned for the rest of that summer

events.note: Tower twenty feet high erected in June 1930 on the highest peak west of Ukiah (Ukiah Dispatch Democrat, June 7, 1930, as transcribed)
Observer M. Hair; a July 19, 1930 report gave July 21 as his first day, and a July 30, 1930 report said the station opened on a Monday with him on duty
August 13, 1930: lookout reported smoke from Pine Mountain near the Sonoma and Mendocino county line; seven acres burned before control
September 3, 1930: lookout detected smoke from a house fire on the Low Gap road; rangers kept it from nearby timber

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A July 19, 1930 report gave July 21 as the observer's first day; a July 30, 1930 report said the station opened on a Monday with M. Hair on duty. The story gives both and does not choose one.
A June 7, 1930 report gives twenty feet for the tower; a June 18, 1930 report gives 20 feet for the building and tower together. The record uses 6.1 m (20 ft) and flags the difference.

sources.title: Lookout Peak in Ukiah, CA, will soon boast 22 miles of MTB trails

notes_for_editor: The 1930 newspaper text comes secondhand, transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page (Ukiah Republican Press and Ukiah Dispatch Democrat); the originals were not checked. The index gives no removal date. Two web searches found no other Lookout Peak history. The trail article is the only source about the peak today and does not mention the station. Index coordinates 39.13617, -123.24596.
